title: NYC Bans AI for Elementary and Middle Schools
paragraphs: New York City, which has the largest public school system in the United States, has banned elementary and middle school students from using generative artificial intelligence tools.

The policy was announced by Mayor Zohran Mamdani on September 2, 2026, shortly before the start of the new school year. According to the mayor's office, it is the most extensive ban of its kind in the country. It is a one-year moratorium that applies to all software using generative AI that is aimed at students up to the eighth grade. During this time, the city will carry out a broader assessment of how children interact with AI. In addition, AI "companion" chatbots, which are designed to act as friends or partners, will be banned for students of all ages.

However, older students will be treated differently. All public high school students will take AI literacy classes twice a year. The city will also launch pilot programs that allow some high school students to use a small number of AI platforms under the supervision of teachers. Meanwhile, teachers will still be allowed to use AI to plan lessons and handle other tasks.

The city also announced new recommendations on screen time. It suggested a daily limit of 30 minutes for students in grades three to five and 45 minutes for those in grades six to eight. Mamdani said that schools should teach children to question ideas and ask why, and that educators have an obligation to do the same with AI.

Reactions have been mixed. Michael Mulgrew, the president of the United Federation of Teachers, welcomed the screen time limits, but said that the AI policy left many questions unanswered. Meanwhile, Josh Golin of the children's advocacy group Fairplay said that a year was not nearly enough time to evaluate AI, and that AI companies should have to prove that their products are effective and safe.
Other school districts are taking similar steps. For example, the Los Angeles school district is temporarily blocking generative AI tools on student devices in all grades while it develops a policy.
